bull_case: N2/A16 plus CoWoS/3DFabric reinforce a multi-layer moat beyond transistor scaling alone.
bear_case: Competitors can narrow process gaps with subsidies and customers can diversify for resilience, raising cost and reducing share at the margin.
thesis: TSMC's moat is widening as leading-edge complexity, packaging and capital requirements rise. Every successful node/packaging ramp compounds process learning, supplier coordination and customer trust.

evidence.claim: 2nm already contributed 3% of 2Q26 wafer revenue during ramp.
2025 capex was about US$40.56B and 2026 guidance US$52B-$56B.

counterevidence: Overseas fabs carry structurally higher costs; customer concentration and Taiwan/export-control tail risks remain material.
unknowns: AI/HPC demand duration beyond the current capacity-constrained cycle
falsifiers: A sustained loss of leading-edge share, repeated yield delays, or owner FCF/share stagnation despite rising capex would weaken the thesis.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: Advanced-node mix, margins and 2026 revenue trends do not show persistent moat shrinkage.

key_kpis.name: owner FCF/share
key_kpis.threshold: sustained growth through the capex cycle

next_checks: 3Q26 results, N2 ramp, CoWoS/advanced packaging capacity, overseas-fab margin, top-customer concentration

subscores.rationale: Node migration, design enablement, yield learning and packaging create high switching costs and support premium economics.
OIP/design enablement, supplier learning, installed capacity and customer tape-out feedback form a compounding manufacturing ecosystem.
Process leadership, yield, packaging and scale provide multiple defenses even as individual node features diffuse.

uncertainties.rationale: AI-cycle duration, overseas economics and geopolitical/customer concentration remain material uncertainties.
